semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source assumes an infinite sequence X₁, X₂, … of real random variables.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target quantifies X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ on a measurable probability space.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The target has an infinite natural-indexed sequence of real random variables on a probability space.

semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes ∀ i, MemLp (X i) 2 μ.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: MemLp 2 faithfully supplies the source's finite-variance condition and the needed integrability.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source assumes identical distribution and a common mean μ.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes ∀ i, IdentDistrib (X i) (X 0) μ μ and centers at ∫ X 0 ∂μ.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: IdentDistrib with X₀ correctly supplies the common law, common expectation, and common variance.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source assumes the sequence is jointly independent as part of i.i.d.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes IndepFun (X i) (X j) μ for every distinct pair i and j.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Pairwise IndepFun is weaker than joint independence, so the target is a genuine strengthening rather than an omission that loses the source case.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source centers the sample mean at the common mean μ.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target subtracts ∫ ω, X 0 ω ∂μ from the normalized sum.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The centered quantity is exactly the sample mean minus the common expectation.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source asks for E|sample mean − μ|.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target integrates the absolute value of the centered sample mean.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Absolute value occurs inside the expectation.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source sums the first N variables.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target sums over Fin (N+1), hence X₀ through X_N.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: Fin (N+1) sums X₀ through X_N, an asymptotically equivalent zero-based encoding of the source's first positive sample sizes.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source sample size is positive because it occurs in 1/N.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target uses N+1 throughout the normalization and comparison rate.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The N+1 normalization avoids division by zero without changing the positive-integer asymptotic statement.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source conclusion is O(1/√N) as N→∞.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target states IsBigO atTop against N ↦ 1 / Real.sqrt (N+1).
semantic_checklist.reasoning: IsBigO at atTop against 1/√(N+1) is exactly an upper O(N⁻¹ᐟ²) assertion.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source requests only an asymptotic upper Big-O estimate.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target concludes only IsBigO and adds no converse estimate or different convergence claim.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The statement does not add a lower bound, asymptotic equivalence, or another mode of convergence.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: The source assumes finite variance but does not require it to be positive.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target assumes MemLp 2 and imposes no nonzero-variance condition.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: The zero-variance case remains included because no positivity condition on the variance is imposed.

semantic_checklist.source_evidence: Every source i.i.d. sequence is identically distributed, jointly independent, and finite-variance.
semantic_checklist.lean_evidence: The target needs identical distribution, square integrability, and only pairwise independence.
semantic_checklist.reasoning: All source cases instantiate the Lean hypotheses, while the Lean theorem additionally covers pairwise-independent non-jointly-independent sequences.

lean_implies_source.reasoning: Joint independence implies pairwise independence, so the Lean theorem specializes to every i.i.d. sequence in the source.

source_implies_lean.reasoning: The source theorem assumes joint independence and therefore does not by itself establish the Lean target's additional pairwise-independent cases.

rationale: Accept as a source-faithful strengthening: the quantity, centering, finite-variance condition, positive sample-size indexing, and Big-O rate agree with Exercise 1.3.3, while pairwise independence makes the theorem strictly more general.
